metadata.title: Thompson (1917) Ch. VII 'The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates' - Plateau / Lamarle tri-junction (120 degree) claim: equations, parameter regimes, Thompson's own figures, and SHA-256-pinned real-specimen micrographs
metadata.organism: species-agnostic ('a true cellular complex, an arrangement of cells in actual physical contact by means of a boundary film', p. 310); specimens: Homo sapiens corneal endothelium; Allium cepa epidermis; Thompson Fig. 103 Zea mays parenchyma; Thompson Fig. 124 Girardia epidermis (after Goebel)

claim.text: Cells in contact, like soap films, meet three-at-a-time at ~120 degrees and in other respects obey Plateau's laws of film configuration.

thompson_quotes.quote: when three similar liquid surfaces meet together, they always do so at an angle of 120 degrees. Whether our two conjoined soap-bubbles be equal or unequal, this is still the invariable rule; because the specific tension of a particular surface is unaffected by any changes of magnitude or form.

(1) If T be equal to T', and t be relatively insignificant, the angles alpha, beta will be of 90 degrees. (2) If T = T', but be a little greater than t, then t will exert an appreciable traction, and alpha, beta will be more than 90 degrees, say, for instance, 100 degrees. (3) If T = T' = t, then alpha, beta, gamma will all equal 120 degrees.

in dividing a closed space into a given number of chambers by means of partition-walls, the least possible area of these partition-walls, taken together, can only be attained when they meet together in groups of three, at equal angles, that is to say at angles of 120 degrees.

in any ordinary section of a vegetable parenchyma, we recognise the appearance of a 'froth' ... in both cases we see the cell-walls everywhere meeting, by threes, at angles of 120 degrees, irrespective of the size of the individual cells: whose relative size, on the other hand, determines the curvature of the partition-walls.

the outer wall of the epidermal cell is exposed to air on the one side, but is in contact with the protoplasm of the cell on the other: and this involves a difference of tensions, so that the outer walls and their adjacent partitions are no longer likely to meet at equal angles of 120 degrees.

This angle, then, of 109 degrees 28' 16'', or very nearly 109 degrees and a half, is the angle at which, in this and every other solid system of liquid films, the edges of the partition-walls meet one another at a point. It is the fundamental angle in the solid geometry of our systems, just as 120 degrees was the fundamental angle of symmetry so long as we considered only the plane projection.

wherever we have, in addition to the forces which tend to produce the regular hexagonal symmetry, some other asymmetrical component arising from growth or traction, then our regular hexagons will be distorted in various simple ways. This condition is illustrated in the accompanying diagram of the epidermis of Girardia.

claim.operational_reading: Thompson's 'about 120 degrees' is explicitly conditional: it holds for INTERIOR walls of equal tension in a system free of asymmetric growth/traction; he himself lists the exceptions (epidermal outer walls, p. 314; growth-distorted epidermis, Fig. 124). The test therefore scores (a) universality of three-fold meeting and (b) closeness of interior angles to 120 degrees, separately, in an isotropic specimen and in an anisotropic one.

E1_lami_tension_balance.statement: Three films with line tensions T1, T2, T3 meeting at a point are in equilibrium when the tension vectors sum to zero; the angle alpha_i opposite film i then satisfies Lami's theorem T1/sin(alpha_1) = T2/sin(alpha_2) = T3/sin(alpha_3), equivalently cos(alpha_i) = (T_i^2 - T_j^2 - T_k^2) / (2 T_j T_k).
E1_lami_tension_balance.existence_condition: T1, T2, T3 must satisfy the triangle inequality; Thompson's water/oil/air example (15, 32, 21 - 'No triangle having sides of these relative magnitudes is possible') has no equilibrium.

E2_plateau_lamarle_minimal_partition.statement: A minimal-length (2D) / minimal-area (3D) partition of a region into N chambers has walls meeting only in threes at 120 degrees (2D) and, in 3D, edges meeting only in fours at arccos(-1/3) = 109 degrees 28' 16''. Four-fold planar vertices are unstable: for a unit square the 'X' partition has length 2*sqrt(2) = 2.828 whereas the two-Y Steiner partition has length 1 + sqrt(3) = 2.732.

E3_angle_sum_identity.statement: At any planar tri-junction alpha + beta + gamma = 360, so the MEAN of the three angles is 120 by identity; the empirical content of the claim lies entirely in the DISPERSION about 120 (and in the absence of 4-fold vertices), not in the mean.
E3_angle_sum_identity.consequence_for_test: Test statistics are the per-vertex Plateau deviation D_v = sqrt(mean_i (theta_i - 120)^2), the pooled SD of theta about 120, the fraction |theta - 120| <= tolerance, and the fraction of vertices that are three-fold.

E4_regular_polygon_vertex_closure.statement: Three regular n-gons close a vertex (3 * interior angle = 360, interior angle = (n-2)*180/n) iff n = 6: Plateau's 120 degree rule and the hexagonal honeycomb are the same statement.

E5_vertex_energy_used_for_simulation.statement: E({r}) = sum_edges Lambda(phi_e) * l_e + sum_cells (K/2) (A_c - A0)^2, with orientation-dependent line tension Lambda(phi) = Lambda0 * (1 + eps * cos 2(phi - phi0)) representing Thompson's 'asymmetrical component arising from growth or traction'. eps = 0 is the Plateau/soap-froth limit (all interior tensions equal -> 120 degrees); eps > 0 distorts angles while keeping vertices three-fold.
E5_vertex_energy_used_for_simulation.source: Farhadifar et al. (2007) Eq. 1 (isotropic form); anisotropic tension after Alt et al. (2017) review

parameters.A0: mean cell area of the seed tessellation

state_variables.theta_i: interior angle i at a tri-cellular vertex (degrees); three per vertex, sum 360
state_variables.f3: fraction of detected vertices at which exactly three cells meet
state_variables.eps: tension anisotropy amplitude (0 = isotropic Plateau froth)
state_variables.n: polygon side number of a cell

boundary_conditions.interior_vs_boundary: Only vertices whose three cells are all fully inside the image (or at least a margin away from the field edge / black circular mask) are scored; Thompson explicitly excludes epidermal outer walls meeting air (p. 314).
boundary_conditions.simulation_domain: periodic square box seeded by a Poisson point process; Voronoi seed tessellation relaxed by gradient descent on E5 without T1 transitions (small strain regime).
boundary_conditions.image_pre-processing: cell-border channel chosen per specimen (max(R,G,B) for alizarin-red corneal endothelium so blue nuclei do not pose as borders; green channel for magenta-walled onion epidermis); line drawings binarised by Otsu.

parameter_regime_table.thompson_case: Fig. 113 case (3); Fig. 103 maize parenchyma; p. 321 pigment epithelium
Fig. 113 case (2): 'alpha, beta ... say, for instance, 100 degrees'

parameter_regime_table.predicted_interior_angles_deg: three-fold vertices persist; angles spread monotonically with eps (Fig. 124 Girardia pattern: ~ (150, 105, 105))

parameter_regime_table.thompson_case: unstable per Plateau/Lamarle; decays into two 120 degree vertices (pp. 309-310)

empirical_biological_claims.claim: Cell walls in parenchyma / epithelia meet by threes (no four-fold vertices).
The three walls meet at ~120 degrees irrespective of cell size.
empirical_biological_claims.testable_as: median |theta - 120| <= 15 degrees and angle SD well below the Poisson-Voronoi null, in an isotropic monolayer

empirical_biological_claims.claim: Asymmetric growth/traction distorts the angles while preserving three-fold meeting.
empirical_biological_claims.testable_as: anisotropic specimen (onion epidermis, Fig. 124) shows larger angle dispersion than the isotropic one, but f3 stays high

empirical_biological_claims.claim: Relative cell size sets wall curvature, not vertex angle.
empirical_biological_claims.testable_as: no correlation between vertex deviation D_v and local cell-area disparity (not scored in this loop; recorded for completeness)

reference_values.poisson_voronoi_null: tri-junction angles of a Poisson-Voronoi tessellation have mean 120 by identity and a broad spread (computed in-script as the negative control; typical SD ~ 20-25 degrees)
reference_values.corneal_endothelium_hexagonality_literat: healthy adult human corneal endothelium is reported with ~55-75 % hexagonal cells (Doughty 1989 review); the mosaic is a classic near-regular tri-junctional monolayer
